q: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as _____ compounds due to their link with organisms.
e: The chemical compounds found in living things are referred to as organic compounds due to their link with organisms. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The enormous molecules termed _____ are formed by smaller molecules connecting together as if they were holding hands.
e: The enormous molecules termed macromolecules are formed by smaller molecules connecting together as if they were holding hands. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: Carbohydrates, proteins, and nucleic acids are natural polymers, while plastics are a type of _____ macromolecules manufactured in the industry.
e: Carbohydrates, proteins, and nucleic acids are natural polymers, while plastics are a type of synthetic macromolecules manufactured in the industry. A polymer is a long chain made by linking many small monomers.

q: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called _____.
e: The simplest organic compounds that contain only the elements carbon and hydrogen are called hydrocarbons. A hydrocarbon contains only carbon and hydrogen.

q: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two _____ groups.
e: An ether is an organic compound with an O atom bonded to two alkyl groups. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the _____.
e: In a symmetrical ether, the two alkyl groups are the same. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Ethers have the general formula _____.
e: Ethers have the general formula CnH2n+2O. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group of an ether are named as an _____ substituent.
e: In the IUPAC system, the oxygen atom and the smaller alkyl group of an ether are named as an alkoxy substituent. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of water from two molecules of alcohol at _____ °C.
e: Ethers can be obtained from alcohol by the elimination of a molecule of water from two molecules of alcohol at 140 °C. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: There is no intermolecular hydrogen bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much _____ than alcohol of similar molecular mass.
e: There is no intermolecular hydrogen bonding between ether molecules, which makes their boiling points much lower than alcohol of similar molecular mass. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.

q: Ethers with up to _____ carbon atoms are soluble in water.
e: Ethers with up to three carbon atoms are soluble in water. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and _____.
e: On heating with concentrated hydrogen iodide (HI), the C-O bond in ethers breaks forming alcohol and alkyl iodide. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.

q: Ethoxyethane was used for many years as a surgical _____ agent but has now been replaced by safer nonflammable alternatives.
e: Ethoxyethane was used for many years as a surgical anaesthetic agent but has now been replaced by safer nonflammable alternatives. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the _____ group.
e: Aldehydes and ketones are organic compounds which contain the carbonyl group. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one _____ atom.
e: In aldehydes, a carbonyl group located at the end of a carbon chain is bonded to at least one hydrogen atom. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula _____.
e: Aldehydes and ketones have the general formula CnH2nO. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: In the IUPAC system for aldehydes, the suffix _____ instead of -e is added to the characteristic stem.
e: In the IUPAC system for aldehydes, the suffix -al instead of -e is added to the characteristic stem. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ketones respectively when gently heated with an oxidising agent such as acidified _____ solution.
e: Primary and secondary alcohols give aldehydes and ketones respectively when gently heated with an oxidising agent such as acidified potassium dichromate solution. In a secondary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to two other carbons.

q: To make the aldehyde, the primary alcohol is heated gently and the product is obtained by _____ to remove it immediately.
e: To make the aldehyde, the primary alcohol is heated gently and the product is obtained by distillation to remove it immediately. In a primary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to only one other carbon, or it is CH3OH.

q: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of $H_2SO_4$ and _____ produces ethanal.
e: The addition of water to ethyne in the presence of H2SO4 and HgSO4 produces ethanal. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: At room temperature, methanal is a gas and ethanal is a volatile _____.
e: At room temperature, methanal is a gas and ethanal is a volatile liquid. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids, but ketones are generally oxidised only under _____ conditions.
e: Aldehydes are easily oxidised to carboxylic acids, but ketones are generally oxidised only under vigorous conditions. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding alcohols using the reducing agent _____ in dry ether.
e: Aldehydes and ketones are easily reduced to the corresponding alcohols using the reducing agent LiAlH4 in dry ether. Ethers have an oxygen bridged between two carbon groups and are often used as solvents.

q: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as _____.
e: Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, adds across the carbon-oxygen double bond in aldehydes and some ketones to produce compounds known as hydroxynitriles. An aldehyde has a carbonyl carbon attached to at least one hydrogen.

q: Formalin, a 40% aqueous solution of _____, is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological specimens.
e: Formalin, a 40% aqueous solution of methanal, is used as a disinfectant and a preservative for biological specimens. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group _____.
e: Carboxylic acids are organic compounds with a carboxyl functional group -COOH. A functional group is the reactive atom grouping that sets the chemistry of an organic family.

q: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a _____ group.
e: The carboxyl group is made up of a carbonyl group and a hydroxyl group. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Carboxylic acids form a homologous series with the general formula _____.
e: Carboxylic acids form a homologous series with the general formula CnH2nO2. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Many carboxylic acid members get their common names from the _____ names of their natural sources.
e: Many carboxylic acid members get their common names from the Latin names of their natural sources. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: In the IUPAC system for carboxylic acids, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by _____.
e: In the IUPAC system for carboxylic acids, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by -oic acid. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the '_____' location position in numbering.
e: Since a carboxylic acid group must always be found at the end of a carbon chain, it is always given the '1' location position in numbering. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Ethanoic acid can be formed by the oxidation of ethanol using atmospheric oxygen in the presence of the bacteria _____.
e: Ethanoic acid can be formed by the oxidation of ethanol using atmospheric oxygen in the presence of the bacteria Acetobacter. Oxidation state tracks how oxidised an atom is; transition metals often show several values.

q: There are intermolecular hydrogen bonds between carboxylic acid molecules, so they have _____ boiling points compared to other compounds of comparable molecular mass.
e: There are intermolecular hydrogen bonds between carboxylic acid molecules, so they have high boiling points compared to other compounds of comparable molecular mass. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.

q: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals to give salt and _____.
e: Carboxylic acids are weak acids, and they can react with reactive metals to give salt and hydrogen. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and _____.
e: Carboxylic acids react with carbonates to give salt, water and carbon dioxide. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using $LiAlH_4$ in _____ ether at room temperature.
e: Carboxylic acids are reduced to their corresponding primary alcohols using LiAlH4 in dry ether at room temperature. In a primary alcohol the carbon that holds OH is attached to only one other carbon, or it is CH3OH.

q: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of _____ acid.
e: The popular painkiller, aspirin, is the acetyl derivative of salicylic acid. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl group has been replaced by an _____ group.
e: Esters are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the hydroxyl group has been replaced by an alkoxy group. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The name of an ester is formed by writing the name of the alkyl group followed by the name of the acid with the -ic acid ending replaced by _____.
e: The name of an ester is formed by writing the name of the alkyl group followed by the name of the acid with the -ic acid ending replaced by -ate. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as _____.
e: Generally, carboxylic acid can react with alcohol to form ester in a process which is known as esterification. Saponification: cations form when atoms lose electrons.

q: Carboxylic acid esters of low molecular mass are colourless, volatile liquids with pleasant _____.
e: Carboxylic acid esters of low molecular mass are colourless, volatile liquids with pleasant odours. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Acidic hydrolysis of an ester is simply the _____ of esterification.
e: Acidic hydrolysis of an ester is simply the reverse of esterification. Esterification is the reaction of an alcohol with an acid to make an ester and water.

q: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, it is fully hydrolysed to form an alcohol and the _____ salt of the carboxylic acid.
e: When an ester is refluxed with an alkali, it is fully hydrolysed to form an alcohol and the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an _____ catalyst.
e: The most common method of transesterification is the reaction of the ester with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst. Transesterification swaps the alkoxy group of an ester with an alcohol to make a different ester.

q: Naturally-occurring esters mixed with NaOH produce _____ that is used for washing dishes and clothes.
e: Naturally-occurring esters mixed with NaOH produce soap that is used for washing dishes and clothes. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of _____ have been replaced by alkyl groups.
e: An amine is a compound in which one or more hydrogen atoms of ammonia have been replaced by alkyl groups. Ammonia: amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Amines are classified as primary, secondary, and tertiary depending on how many _____ groups are attached to the nitrogen.
e: Amines are classified as primary, secondary, and tertiary depending on how many alkyl groups are attached to the nitrogen. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: In the IUPAC system for amines, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by _____.
e: In the IUPAC system for amines, the -e from the name of the parent chain is replaced by -amine. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in _____.
e: Ethanamine is prepared by heating bromoethane with an excess of ammonia dissolved in ethanol. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Excess hot ethanolic ammonia is used in amine preparation to avoid the formation of secondary and tertiary amines and _____ salts.
e: Excess hot ethanolic ammonia is used in amine preparation to avoid the formation of secondary and tertiary amines and ammonium salts. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Liquid amines possess a _____ smell.
e: Liquid amines possess a fishy smell. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Primary and secondary amines have higher boiling points than alkanes because they can form an intermolecular _____ bonding.
e: Primary and secondary amines have higher boiling points than alkanes because they can form an intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Intermolecular forces tug neighbouring molecules or ions together; they are not the bonds inside a molecule.

q: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell, known as the _____ reaction.
e: Ethanamine reacts with chloroform in the presence of an alkali to form ethyl isocyanide with an unpleasant smell, known as the carbylamine reaction. An amine is an organic base with nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by an _____ group.
e: Amides are carboxylic acid derivatives in which the -OH of the carboxylic acid has been replaced by an amine group. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Amides are named as derivatives of the corresponding carboxylic acids, the suffix -amide being substituted for _____ in the name of the parent acid.
e: Amides are named as derivatives of the corresponding carboxylic acids, the suffix -amide being substituted for -oic acid in the name of the parent acid. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: The addition of ammonia to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a _____ reaction, as water is eliminated.
e: The addition of ammonia to a carboxylic acid forms an amide via a condensation reaction, as water is eliminated. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Like esters, aqueous solutions of amides are usually _____.
e: Like esters, aqueous solutions of amides are usually neutral. An ester has the -COO- link and is often made from an acid plus an alcohol.

q: If an amide is refluxed with hydrochloric acid, the products are the corresponding carboxylic acid and a primary _____.
e: If an amide is refluxed with hydrochloric acid, the products are the corresponding carboxylic acid and a primary amine. Carboxylic acids contain the -COOH group and are typically weak acids.

q: Amides such as nylon are used in textiles, to produce ropes, bulletproof vests and _____ cords.
e: Amides such as nylon are used in textiles, to produce ropes, bulletproof vests and tyre cords. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.
